answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: I could not find a standalone, publicly posted Blue Cross NC 'medical policy' document that states specific medical-necessity criteria for unicompartmental/partial knee arthroplasty (CPT 27446). Blue Cross NC's provider site states that it discontinued its public medical-policy search tool for many services and now uses licensed MCG (Milliman Care Guidelines) Care Guidelines, administered through the 'MCG Cite Guideline Transparency (CGT) Portal,' for medical-necessity review. Per Blue Cross NC's own site: 'The medical policy search tool is no longer active. Publicly accessible medical policies can be found in the Alphabetical and Categorical listings below. Guidelines that are not publicly accessible can be viewed by logging in to the MCG Cite Guideline Transparency (CGT) Portal.' A knee-arthroplasty-specific MCG guideline was not found among Blue Cross NC's publicly listed 'Commercial Surgery' policy updates I was able to retrieve (which instead cover adjacent topics like patient-specific instrumentation and computer-assisted navigation, not the core indications for CPT 27446). Because federal ACA claims-and-appeals regulations (29 CFR 2560.503-1 / 45 CFR 147.136) require that, on request, the plan disclose the specific internal rule, guideline, protocol, or criterion relied upon in a denial (or a statement that none exists), the patient/provider should: (1) call the number on the back of the member ID card or the number in the denial letter and explicitly request, in writing, 'the specific medical policy, clinical guideline, or MCG care guideline criteria applied to deny CPT 27446 for this member, including the guideline number/title/version'; (2) ask the treating orthopedic surgeon's office (or the patient, via an authorized representative) to request MCG Cite Guideline Transparency Portal access/printout for the specific 'Knee Arthroplasty' guideline used in this determination; and (3) request this at the same time the appeal is filed, since Blue Cross NC is obligated to provide it as part of the adverse benefit determination and appeal process.

I was not able to locate and read the actual text of the MCG 'Knee Arthroplasty' guideline (or an equivalent public BCBSNC document) that Blue Cross NC applied to this CPT 27446 denial, so I cannot quote its medical-necessity criteria. A similarly named 'Knee Arthroplasty' MCG-based guideline exists publicly for a different Blue plan (BCBS Florida, mcgs.bcbsfl.com), but that is a different license/company's implementation and cannot be assumed to be identical to what Blue Cross NC applied to this North Carolina commercial member — I am not naming it as the governing document here because I could not confirm it is the same version/criteria Blue Cross NC used.
